_comment: WP2b-1 TASK 2 — setup-parameter registry. One entry per tunable: identity, value space, direction semantics, typical window, change effort, physical mechanism, optional phase affinity, notes, recommendation_target. 'maps_to' entries prefixed 'setup_parameters.car.*' for arb_front_mount/tc_lat/tc_lon/abs_position are NEW car.json fields, created in TASK 3 (not yet present). Every entry with a config/car_data.json lookup cites the exact section in 'notes' and had its direction_semantics cross-checked against that section's actual digitised values (not assumed from the original task wording) — see the tc_lat/tc_lon correction and the abs_position categorical rewrite as the two cases where the check changed the entry. 'value_source': 'setup_sheet' (default, maps_to is a real car.json path) vs 'logged_data' (maps_to is null -- the parameter's truth is a logged channel, not a setup-sheet field; value_source and recommendation_target are independent axes).

arb_fl.label: Front-Left ARB Position

typical_window.notes: 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused; rear usually a slightly lower position than front

arb_fl.mechanism: Sets front-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets front lateral-load-transfer share, which sets front grip share relative to rear.
arb_fl.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.front (6.3..20.6 N/mm at drop link, ratio_to_wheel 1.07) -- verified: position 1->6.3 N/mm, position 7->20.6 N/mm, monotonic increasing, confirms 1=softest. Position-to-stiffness convention (linear vs squared) unresolved -- flagged convention_unresolved, resolve in WP5b. Four fully independent per-corner targets, no pairing concept.

arb_fr.label: Front-Right ARB Position

typical_window.notes: 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused; rear usually a slightly lower position than front

arb_fr.mechanism: Sets front-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets front lateral-load-transfer share, which sets front grip share relative to rear.
arb_fr.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.front. Four fully independent per-corner targets, no pairing concept.

arb_rl.label: Rear-Left ARB Position

arb_rl.mechanism: Sets rear-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets rear lateral-load-transfer share, which sets rear grip share relative to front.
arb_rl.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.rear (26.9..80.1 N/mm at drop link, ratio_to_wheel 0.77) -- verified: position 1->26.9 N/mm, position 7->80.1 N/mm, monotonic increasing, confirms 1=softest. Same convention_unresolved flag as front.

arb_rr.label: Rear-Right ARB Position

typical_window.notes: usually a slightly lower position than front; 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused

arb_rr.mechanism: Sets rear-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets rear lateral-load-transfer share, which sets rear grip share relative to front.

arb_front_mount.label: Front ARB Mount
arb_front_mount.mechanism: Upright mount couples steering input to ARB preload -- higher position gives a more direct/snappy turn-in response.
arb_front_mount.notes: No source image digitises this parameter -- mechanism from team knowledge only, no car_data.json cross-check available. NEW car.json field, added to the existing 'car' dict (no separate front_axle tier -- schema decision, TASK 3) alongside differential_position/wing_position/splitter_offset.

springs_front.label: Front Springs
springs_front.mechanism: Sets front-axle vertical (ride) stiffness independent of roll stiffness; conditions which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) is valid.
springs_front.notes: Damper matrix conditions the recommended damper windows on the installed spring pairing -- see dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing, cells keyed '{front}x{rear}'.

springs_rear.label: Rear Springs
springs_rear.mechanism: Sets rear-axle vertical (ride) stiffness independent of roll stiffness; conditions which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) is valid.

damper_bump_ls_fl.label: FL Bump Low-Speed
damper_bump_ls_fl.mechanism: Controls body motion into the damper (dive, roll rate at turn-in) -- platform control.
damper_bump_ls_fl.notes: Click semantics confirmed by car_data.json dampers.dyno_metadata.front.click_semantics (dyno chart's own '0-0-0-0'/'18-18-18-18' reference curves). Team practice: axle-symmetric values, 1-2 click changes, bump/rebound moved independently to counter specific effects.

damper_blowoff_fl.label: FL Blowoff
damper_blowoff_fl.mechanism: Caps peak force at high shaft speed -- contact-patch protection over the worst hits; 0 means no relief is given, a deliberate platform-over-protection choice.

damper_rebound_ls_fl.label: FL Rebound Low-Speed
damper_rebound_ls_fl.mechanism: Controls platform recovery speed after compression -- floating control.

damper_rebound_hs_fl.label: FL Rebound High-Speed
damper_rebound_hs_fl.mechanism: Controls wheel-release after kerbs; too stiff jacks the car down and unloads the tyre.

ride_height_front.label: Front Ride Height
ride_height_front.mechanism: Sets front floor/splitter proximity to the ground -- aero platform height; FIA and aero conventions quoted at a constant offset, aero wears so the measured value is used to verify, not independently settable.
ride_height_front.notes: Convention offsets: car_data.json ride_height_measuring_points (FIA/ADAC/Porsche-laser, per corner X/Y/Z). Not itself a free target -- both readings move together.

ride_height_rear.label: Rear Ride Height
ride_height_rear.mechanism: Sets rear floor/diffuser exit height -- aero platform height and rake (with ride_height_front); FIA and aero conventions quoted at a constant offset.

diff_package.label: Differential Package
diff_package.mechanism: Selects the spring/ramp preload package that determines the diff's locking-torque-vs-position curve (see diff_position).
diff_package.notes: Reference curve: car_data.json diff_locking_torque (installed_package '8304N_1372N_30-5'). ~2h to change; context only, not a session-level target.

diff_position.label: Differential Position
diff_position.mechanism: Sets clutch-pack preload/locking torque on the installed diff package -- more locking torque resists axle-speed difference under power, affecting exit rotation vs. traction.
diff_position.notes: Locking torque lookup: car_data.json diff_locking_torque.positions (30-5 package: 1->70 Nm .. 5->250 Nm, monotonic increasing) -- verified, confirms 1=least. NEW car.json fields required: measured locking torque (Nm) per position 1-5 on the setup sheet (drifts with wear, measured continuously) -- TASK 3.

wing_position.label: Wing Position
wing_position.mechanism: Rear wing angle sets rear downforce -- affects high-speed balance (more angle = more rear grip/stability, less top speed).
wing_position.notes: Legal set confirmed against car_data.json wing_position_table's 'GT3 R 2026' column: only 7.3/8.3/9.3 deg (P8/P9/P10) have an entry -- corrected from the original P9|P10|P11 draft.

toe_front.label: Front Toe
toe_front.mechanism: Front toe-out sharpens initial turn-in response at the cost of straight-line stability and tyre wear.
toe_front.notes: No digitised car_data table backs this parameter's direction (the toe-vs-wheel-travel kinematic curves were pruned as no-consumer) -- value space/direction from team knowledge only.

toe_rear.label: Rear Toe
toe_rear.mechanism: Rear toe-in adds straight-line and corner-exit stability at the cost of some rear tyre wear.
toe_rear.notes: Team knowledge only, no car_data table backing (same as toe_front).

camber_fl.label: FL Camber
camber_fl.mechanism: Sets static camber -- dictated by tyre usage/temperature distribution across the contact patch.
camber_fl.notes: Base -3.5 deg front. Team knowledge only, no car_data table backing (camber-vs-wheel-travel curves were pruned as no-consumer). WP2b-2: step 0.3deg added from the engineer decision matrix (US-APX-high/OS-APX-high camber cells) -- not previously in the team-knowledge registry pass, no car_data.json table to cross-check against; treat as elicited pending engineering review. CORRECTED 2026-07-26 (matrix v2, project-lead review): step is 0.1deg, not the 0.3deg WP2b-2 elicited-default -- typical field practice is a 0.2deg change (two 0.1deg clicks); a tyre-surface/wear-pattern inspection is a precondition before applying any camber change, and a one-sided (single-corner) change is sometimes preferred over the symmetric FL+FR pair the recommendation rules encode -- both noted in the citing rules' rationale text.

tc_lat.label: Traction Control - Lateral

direction_semantics.1: driver modulation, minimal TC support (wording near-identical to 0; the scale is not cleanly monotonic between 0/1 and 2 -- see notes)
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted car rotation under lateral load on power = MORE TC intervention/support

typical_window.notes: 5 = 'normal conditions' per source table; increase toward 11 for more support, decrease toward 2 for more permitted rotation

tc_lat.mechanism: Sets how much car rotation the TC system permits during the lateral-loaded cornering phase (power applied while cornering); higher position = less permitted rotation = more intervention.
tc_lat.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel (changed on feel, tyre life, fuel load) -- truth is a logged-data trace, not a setup-sheet value; switch-position channel name TBD, identify in next data file's channel scan. CORRECTED after review -- direction is the OPPOSITE of a naive 'higher position = more rotation allowed' reading. Verified against car_data.json tc (source TC_reference.png, current LAT/LON system): position 2 = 'even more rotation', 3 = 'increased rotation', 4 = 'slightly more rotation', 5 = 'normal conditions', 6 = 'less rotation', 8-9 = 'increased TC support', 10 = 'strongly increased TC support', 11 = 'lots of TC support' -- monotonically LESS rotation permitted from 2 through 11. Position 1's wording ('driver modulation, little TC support') is near-identical to 0's, i.e. the 0/1 pair reads as a low-intervention state adjacent to the numeric floor rather than continuing the 2-11 trend -- flagged, not smoothed over. Supersedes the 2023-25 single-switch TC_1.png system (not digitised).

tc_lon.label: Traction Control - Longitudinal

direction_semantics.0: driver modulation, little TC support -- NOTE: per project docs, TC LON at 0 does NOT disable TC (only TC LAT=0 does); wording matches position 1
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted wheel spin under longitudinal load = MORE TC intervention/support

tc_lon.mechanism: Sets how much wheel spin the TC system permits during high-torque longitudinal phases (1st/2nd gear power-down on exit); higher position = less permitted spin = more intervention, useful for managing rear-tyre degradation.
tc_lon.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel (changed on feel, tyre life, fuel load) -- truth is a logged-data trace, not a setup-sheet value; switch-position channel name TBD, identify in next data file's channel scan. CORRECTED alongside tc_lat -- same direction check applied: verified against car_data.json tc, monotonically less wheel spin permitted from 2 through 11, 5 = baseline. TC LON=0-does-not-switch-off-TC is stated in the (non-digitised) TC_1.png introductory text and is architecturally still true for the current system (only TC LAT has an off state).

abs_position.label: ABS Position

direction_semantics.type: categorical, NOT a single monotonic soft/hard axis
direction_semantics.1_to_8: dry maps -- 1-4 grouped 'High' overall grip level (1=baseline dry-high, 2/4=more stable FA/RA variants, 3=printed 'BL Medium grip map' despite its own row being categorised 'High' -- verified as printed, not a transcription error), 5-8 grouped 'Medium' overall grip level (5=baseline medium, 6=more stable, 7-8=add lateral support)
direction_semantics.9_to_11: wet maps ascending severity -- 9=baseline good-wet-grip, 10=rain tyres/heavy wet (limited deceleration), 11=monsoon emergency (highly limited deceleration)

abs_position.mechanism: Selects the ABS intervention map; team practice is a sweet-spot search within the dry or wet bracket appropriate to conditions, not a linear soft-to-hard sweep.
abs_position.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel (changed on feel, tyre life, fuel load) -- truth is a logged-data trace, not a setup-sheet value; switch-position channel name TBD, identify in next data file's channel scan. Installed config V2 (verified: ABS_2.png header reads 'Map for ABS configuration option "V2"'). Full table: car_data.json abs. Monza2/CTMP/V4 not digitised (not installed) -- archived in docs/car_data/ only. SUPERSEDED-IN-PRACTICE ANNOTATION 2026-07-26 (matrix v2, project-lead review) -- NOT a deletion of the direction_semantics finding above, which remains true (abs_position is categorical, not one monotonic axis, and jumping across grip-level brackets, e.g. position 4 to 9, is still nonsensical). What is superseded in practice: WITHIN one grip-level bracket, an ordinal +1/+2 step IS used as a practical stability lever by the matrix v2 rules (see config/recommendations.json US-BRK-low-esc, INST-BRK-low) -- 'try-and-error' nudges toward the front- or rear-axle-stable variant, not a claim that the whole 0-11 range is monotonic. See those rules' rationale for the elicitation context.

brake_bias.label: Brake Bias
brake_bias.mechanism: Driver-exclusive in-corner adjustment; not a setup-sheet target.
brake_bias.notes: Value read from logged data, not set on the setup sheet -- brake bias channel name TBD, identify in next data file's channel scan.

splitter_offset.label: Splitter Offset
splitter_offset.mechanism: Front aero balance trim; context only in this WP.
splitter_offset.notes: No car_data digitisation -- context entry per task scope.

kinematic_variants.label: Kinematic Variants
kinematic_variants.mechanism: Homologated suspension-geometry variants (front FS-series, rear RS-series); background context for interpreting damper ratio / roll centre / antidive-antisquat behaviour, not a session-level tunable.

gear_ratios.label: Gear Ratios
gear_ratios.mechanism: Fixed per-event gearbox setup; context only in this WP.
gear_ratios.notes: Not digitised into car_data.json -- no near-term consumer (stub there, reason: context-only). Source: docs/car_data/Gear_ratio.png.
